clue.text: Taken in? Get cheat prosecuted, pocketing millions

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat or swindle them

indicators.note: pocketing means the word for prosecuted holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: to sue someone is to take them to court, so prosecuted gives SUED
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A question about being fooled, then an urge to have a crooked swindler taken to court for stealing millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketing' puts M inside SUED, giving SUMED after CON. 'Taken in' means eaten or swallowed, not fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been eaten has been taken in by the body, so the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Check cocaine in six deliveries

indicators.note: in means the cocaine letter is set inside the cricket phrase

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled, so six deliveries make one over
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: Drugs are found during a short spell of cricket bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler delivers the ball six times in an over, so 'six deliveries' is ONE OVER. 'in' puts C inside ONE, making ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick inspection is a once-over, so a check is a synonym.

clue.text: Run film

explanation.definitionFit: To shoot along is to run or rush swiftly, and to shoot a movie is to film it.

clue.text: Religious figure, the prior, involving us with Rome

indicators.note: involve once meant to roll up or entwine, so the words are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A monastery's prior gets caught up with a group of us and the Roman church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but it scrambles THE PRIOR, US and ROME together.
explanation.definitionFit: The head nun of a convent is a religious figure, so the title fits the general description.

clue.text: One of those settlers, perhaps

parts.note: settlers sound like colonists, but here they are things that settle a contest, such as a final game

explanation.surface: Someone who emigrated to colonise new land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlers' makes you think of pioneers; it means something that settles a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciding game settles who wins, so it is one example of a thing that settles a contest.

clue.text: Title page

explanation.definitionFit: To title someone is to name them, as in calling them a hero, and to page someone is to summon them over a speaker.

clue.text: Exotic garment for child

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Exotic garment for child (9)', gives no wordplay for CHEONGSAM: 'for child' supplies none of its letters, so the clue looks cut short or garbled in the OCR and no scan is held.

clue.text: They're not used to taking orders

definitions.text: They're not used to taking orders

parts.words: They're not used to taking orders
parts.note: orders sounds like commands to obey, but here it means holy orders, entered by priests on ordination

explanation.surface: People who dislike being bossed about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking orders' reads as obeying instructions; in the church, taking holy orders means becoming a priest, which these people have not done.
explanation.definitionFit: Church members who are not ordained clergy are the laity, people outside holy orders.

clue.text: Inept on skis, no? Promptly ace is called in to show expertise

indicators.note: called in means the following pieces are brought inside the scrambled letters
inept means clumsy or badly done, so the letters are arranged clumsily into a new order

parts.note: promptly means at once, right now
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A clumsy skier is asked whether a champion should be summoned at once to demonstrate real skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inept' rearranges ONSKISNO into KSONIONS, and 'called in' puts NOW and ONE inside it after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: To know one's onions is a British idiom for knowing one's subject thoroughly, which shows expertise.

clue.text: Address from a Conservative on tariff

parts.note: a tariff is a charge or cost

explanation.surface: A speech given by a Tory politician about import duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a noun for a speech, but it is the verb: to speak to someone directly.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to go up and speak to them, a verb sense of address.

clue.text: French resort's short railway supplying food factory

indicators.note: short means the resort name is cut by its last letter

parts.note: Cannes is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A small branch line from a Riviera town carries produce to a processing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts CANNES to CANNE, which RY then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant where food is sealed into tins is a factory processing food.

clue.text: Substantial walls in the British seaside town

indicators.note: walls means the word for substantial surrounds the other piece like a wall

parts.note: a sound argument is solid and substantial

explanation.surface: Big walls stand around a resort on the British coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walls' puts SOUND around THE. Southend-on-Sea is a seaside resort in Essex, east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Southend-on-Sea is a resort on the Thames estuary in Essex, a classic English seaside town.

clue.text: Ramble round about, led by staff

indicators.note: led by means the following piece comes after the word for staff

parts.note: a wand is a slender rod or staff

indicators.note: round means the word for about is turned back to front

parts.note: re is Latin for about, regarding

explanation.surface: A walker goes round in circles, guided by a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns RE into ER, which comes after WAND because it is 'led by staff'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramble is to stroll aimlessly, a synonym of roaming about.

clue.text: Wild threats by gangs evoking emotions

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a ring is a gang of criminals, such as a drug ring

explanation.surface: Gangsters issuing savage threats stir up people's feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges THREATS into HEARTST, and RINGS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The heartstrings are a figure for one's deepest feelings, as in tugging at them.

clue.text: Usable stock

explanation.definitionFit: Something ready-made can be used straight away, and a stock phrase is a ready-made, unoriginal one.

clue.text: Turns up loaded with favourite quotations

indicators.note: loaded with means the reversed word carries the other piece inside it
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: turns are spins
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone appears weighed down with their best-loved sayings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SPINS into SNIPS, and 'loaded with' puts PET inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Short extracts quoted from a text are fragments or snippets.

clue.text: Introduce pieces on piano in suitable evaluation

indicators.note: in means the pieces are placed inside the word for suitable

parts.note: apt means suitable

indicators.note: on means the following words come after the musical letter

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to raise a subject is to introduce it
chessmen are pieces, so pieces gives MEN

explanation.surface: Advice to play some compositions on the piano for a fitting assessment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets RAISE and MEN after P, and 'in' puts that run inside APT, splitting it AP...T.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisement is an older word for an appraisal, a valuation or assessment.

clue.text: Accountant, deployed, charged

parts.note: something deployed has been put to use

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper sent out on duty is billed for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' tempts as an anagram signal; it simply means USED.
explanation.definitionFit: A person charged with a crime is the defendant, formally called the one indicted.

clue.text: Builder responsible for stack in past

indicators.note: in means the word for stack goes inside the word for past

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by
a rick is a stack of hay

explanation.surface: A tradesman who built a chimney stack in years gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stack' suggests a chimney; it is a hayrick. A bricky is British slang for a bricklayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bricky is informal British slang for a bricklayer, a kind of building worker.

clue.text: Older German interrupted by Spanish king

indicators.note: interrupted by means the German abbreviation is broken open by the other piece

parts.note: rey is Spanish for king

explanation.surface: An elderly German has his talk cut short by the King of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted by' puts REY inside GER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair turns grey with age, so someone with more grey hair is likely more aged.

clue.text: Try prisoner, at first showing scorn for court?

indicators.note: at first means the word for prisoner comes at the front

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
to tempt is an old sense of to try or test, as in tempting fate

explanation.surface: Putting a convict on trial and displaying disdain for the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: contempt of court is disrespect for a court's authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt means scorn, and contempt of court is the offence of showing it to a court.

clue.text: Compound interest errors will show

indicators.note: will show means the letters are on display inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Mistakes in calculating compound interest will become apparent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' attaches to 'interest' in the surface, but it is the definition: a chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Carriage mostly lined with flash leather

indicators.note: lined with means the shortened carriage holds the other piece inside it
mostly means the carriage word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chaise is a light horse-drawn carriage
a mo is a moment, a flash, as in half a mo

explanation.surface: A coach with most of its interior fitted out in showy leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts CHAISE to CHAIS, and 'lined with' puts MO inside it. 'flash' looks like an adjective for showy; it is a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamois is soft leather from the skin of the mountain goat, used for polishing cloths.

clue.text: It's enough to make one start

definitions.text: It's enough to make one start

parts.words: It's enough to make one start
parts.note: start sounds like a jump of fright, but here it is a beginning

explanation.surface: Something alarming enough to make you jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make one start' sounds like being startled; it means the beginning itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset of something is its very beginning.

clue.text: Individual kidney

explanation.definitionFit: An odd individual is an odd sort, and kidney is an old word for kind or sort, as in people of that kidney.

clue.text: Trouble I had about accent

indicators.note: about means the contraction for I had is turned round

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
an accent on a syllable is its stress

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having had a problem with their pronunciation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ID into DI, which STRESS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is suffering or anguish, a synonym of trouble.
